newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil says 1996 net profit tops three trln rbls.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil says 1996 net profit tops three trln rbls.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil said on Wednesday its 1996 net profit, according to preliminary estimates, was over three trillion roubles after 2.4 trillion roubles in 1995.
Net profit for the parent company alone, excluding subsidiaries, was 1.3 trillion roubles after 330 billion in 1995, it said in a statement.
The statement clarified remarks by LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov who said on Tuesday that LUKoil's net profit in 1996 was 1.3 trillion roubles.
LUKoil reiterated that pre-tax profit in 1996 would be over 3.7 trillion roubles. Pre-tax profit in 1995 was 3.43 trillion roubles.
A LUKoil spokesman said he was unable to comment on a figure for 1996 sales of 35 trillion roubles given by Alekperov. On Monday the company said the value of its 1996 output was 41 trillion roubles.
Sales in the first nine months of this year were 32.56 trillion roubles, up from 13.80 trillion in the same 1995 period.
OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil has now released the following preliminary data, according to Russian accounting standards, for 1996, over the past few days.
NOTES - 1997 figures are planned, 1996 figures are preliminary estimates.
LUKoil has not yet published figures to international accounting standards, but has appointed international auditing firm KPMG to prepare such figures.

Russian accounting standards differ significantly from those normally supplied in the West. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
